messages:
Maya (Support): FYI incoming request from ACME Studios (acct acme-459). They asked for a quota bump for embeddings: current monthly cap 500k -> requested 5M. Spotted unusual bursts in last 24h. Handing off for fraud screening before product/backlog can consider.

Liam (Sales): @Maya thanks — they're on a paid Pro plan, signed yesterday. This is a POC for a big potential deal, need runway. Can we expedite? :pray:

Maya (Support): Billing looks good, payment method valid. Logs show multiple big bursts (50k tokens) from 3 distinct IPs, repeated every ~10m. Also saw increased 429s earlier.

Carlos (FraudOps): Looping in FraudOps. Can you paste the raw request IDs / sample payloads + timestamps and the IPs? We'll run our heuristics and ASN lookups. Also need account creation timestamp.

Maya (Support): Paste below — truncated example payloads and headers for privacy:
```
request_id: r-8521c
acct: acme-459
time: 2026-02-17T14:02:21Z
ip: 34.82.11.203 (us-central1)
model: embed-1-large
tokens: 48620
payload: {"items":["..."], "metadata":{}}
```
Created: 2026-02-16T09:12:04Z

Aisha (Product): If FraudOps clears, Product can approve a temporary quota with strict controls. Proposal: grant a time-limited increase (48–72h), enforce per-minute rate cap, enable streaming watchdog alerts, and require CSM touchpoint. Need rollout criteria: clear fraud score + signed contact.

Liam (Sales): Customer asks for 24–72h. Suggest +5x temporary with 5 min token window and webhook alerts to their SRE. Will provide org contact info if needed.

Carlos (FraudOps): I'll run the checks. Screening steps:
- account creation/age
- payment anomalies
- IP/ASN reputation
- model + payload fingerprinting
- replay/automation pattern detection
ETA: ~2 hours. Creating FRD ticket.

investigation-bot: Created FRD ticket FRD-9042 and Incident INC-2026 for tracking. Assigned: Carlos.

Carlos (FraudOps): Quick findings: IPs map to a known proxy ASN, same API key used in 3 other accounts created in last week. Payloads show near-identical embeds with minor variances — automation pattern likely. Flagging as suspicious.

Liam (Sales): Hmm that's concerning. Customer says they run on a managed puppeteer cluster for data ingest — they can provide a signed PO and company domain. If they provide org proof + contact, can we do conditional approval?

Aisha (Product): Product position: conditional approval only. Options:
- If KYC provided (org email + PO): allow +3x for 72h with 60 req/min limit + active monitoring and daily review.
- If no proof: deny increase and require throttling and application-level retries.
We need a documented rollback trigger (fraud score > 0.7 or anomaly rate > 5%).

Carlos (FraudOps): Agreed. Also recommend forcing origin verification (restrict API key to their IPs) and enable session-based token binding for the window. If they can't bind, keep denied.

Maya (Support): Action items recap:
- Carlos: finish FRD-9042 screening, post summary in this thread (ETA 2h)
- Liam: collect org domain + signed PO + point-of-contact
- Aisha: draft conditional quota template + rollback criteria
I'll hold the request pending FRD outcome.

Liam (Sales): On it — CSM will get PO and org email within 90m.

Carlos (FraudOps): Update: After deeper look, additional accounts share API key patterns — however the customer provided a signed PO + org email and confirmed they run through a third-party proxy. We still see proxy ASN traffic. Recommendation: conditional approval limited to +3x tokens for 72h, require IP allowlist + 60 req/min rate cap, enable alerting to #security and Sales, daily fraud summary to Sales/Product. If anomalies spike, automatic revoke.

Aisha (Product): That's acceptable. I'll prepare the conditional quota config and the rollback playbook. Also add a requirement: webhook to CSM on anomalies and an agreed evaluation prompt set to check quality regressions.

Maya (Support): Implementing: created ticket SUP-6142 to apply +3x quota, set rate limit 60 req/min, enabled monitoring hooks to #security and customer webhook. FRD-9042 summary attached.

deploy-bot: SUP-6142 applied to acme-459 in staging; monitoring alerts active.

Carlos (FraudOps): Final note: This is temporary (72h). If daily fraud score stays <0.25 and no automation fingerprints escalate, we can consider extending to the requested level but only after Product review.

Liam (Sales): Thanks team — will keep the customer informed and collect any additional telemetry. :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): Closing handoff for now. Reopen thread if anything changes.
